# ADR-055 — Service monitoring is worker-owned; the worker-heartbeat watchdog is API-owned

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Service monitoring is worker-owned; the worker-heartbeat watchdog is API-owned.** `monitor_targets` / `monitor_checks` / `monitor_incidents` are server-configured and driven by a worker cron covering HTTP status, latency, timeout, interval, consecutive-failure threshold, recovery threshold, TLS-expiry warning and maintenance windows. **Consecutive-failure counting is derived from `monitor_checks`, never stored as a counter column** — `apps/worker/src/health/breaker.ts`'s argument applies verbatim: a counter is a second source of truth that must be reset correctly on every success path, whereas reading the last N rows cannot drift. **An incident, by contrast, is legitimate durable state**, because it carries acknowledgement and is the anchor that makes a *second* outage notifiable. Alert dedupe keys are therefore **incident-scoped** — `monitor:${incidentId}:opened` and `:resolved` — which is the fix for a real latent defect this decision is written against: `notification_dispatch_log.dedupe_key` is a permanent primary key with no TTL, and the existing `calendar-needs-reauth:${connectionId}` producer carries no time or incident discriminator, so once that key is `accepted` the connection can never alert again. **The worker cannot alert on its own death**, so the `worker_heartbeat` staleness check — the half of `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "alert on staleness" mandate that was never built — **belongs to the API process**, not to a worker job; all other monitoring remains worker-owned. The residual blind spot, a hung or crash-looping worker behind a healthy API, is documented rather than papered over. Monitoring reuses the notification router unchanged: `category: "alert"` is already wired end to end, already defaults `notify_alerts = true`, and is already exempt from quiet hours, so **no new notification category and no `devices` column are added**. Uptime is a **three-state** model — `up` / `down` / `not_checked` — enforced by the same structural refine `HealthMetricPointSchema` uses, so a window in which the monitor was not running can never render as `0%`. Targets are seeded from verified Personal OS services only; whether the worker container can reach the Tailscale Serve routes from a plain bridge network is **unverified and must be proven in Checkpoint 7.5**, and if it cannot, the Serve/TLS layer is recorded as an explicit blind spot rather than assumed covered (Phase 7 Checkpoint 7.0, user-approved 2026-08-30) **[Present state corrected by ADR-057.]**
